newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open 0.22 percent higher.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open 0.22 percent higher.

text.p: French shares opened 0.22 percent higher on Wednesday as Wall Street's 135 point gain had already been matched in Paris on Tuesday, dealers said.

Wall Street closed 135.25 points, or 2.10 percent, higher in the wake of favourable March CPI data, while Paris had ended Tuesday with a 2.12 percent gain, also benefitting from the CPI and the firmer dollar.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index was u 3.27 points or 0.12 percent at 2,623.90 at 0807 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract was up at 2,628 from 2,626 on Tuesday's close. Investors awaiting U.S. March industrial production at 1315 GMT.
The dollar was subdued on Wednesday which could lead to some profit-taking on dollar earners such as Elf Aquitaine, dealers said.
"There is a general lack of interest and volumes are very low. With these swings and roundabouts people do not know what way the market is going next," a broker said.
BIC was 4.85 percent higher at 887 francs on the back of a proposed two-for-one stock spliy in July.
Coflexip led the losers with a 3.27 percent decline to 322.10 francs. Coflexip has risen steadily recently.
Total, up 0.02 percent at 470, plans to sell 55 percent in TOPNA to Ultramar Diamond Shamrock for a stake in Ultramar.
